title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 50
paragraphs: So far they went at that time; and when the appointed day arrived for the answer, and they had come to the place agreed upon, Cleomenes asked Aristagoras how many days' journey it was from the Ionian sea to the residence of the king. Now Aristagoras, who in other respects acted cleverly and deceived him well, in this point made a mistake: for whereas he should not have told him the truth, at least if he wished to bring the Spartans out to Asia, he in fact said that it was a journey up from the sea of three months. The other cut short the rest of Aristagoras's account of the way and said: “Milesian guest-friend, get yourself out of Sparta before the sun sets; for you speak a word that sounds not well in Lacedaemonian ears, wanting to take them on a three months' journey from the sea.”
